_note: Adversarial stress-test of an EXISTING idea. The load-bearing things under test: it ATTACKS (assumptions/failure modes/alternatives/cost) rather than helping build; it asks ONE question at a time and waits; each question carries a recommended answer/stance; it looks up facts itself but puts decisions to the user; it does NOT produce code/plan/artifacts (hands off instead); and it stays in the stress-test lane rather than sliding into design-gate's produce-a-plan job. Temperament (lead with the objection, no cushioning) is the point that separates it from design-gate.

evals.name: attacks-one-question-at-a-time-with-a-stance
evals.prompt: Grill me on this: I'm going to add a Redis cache in front of our session lookups to cut latency.
evals.expected_output: Opens by attacking a soft spot (e.g. cache invalidation / stale sessions on logout, the added failure mode when Redis is down, whether latency is actually the bottleneck) — leading with the objection, not praise. Asks ONE question and stops for the answer. The question carries a recommended answer / stance, not a blank prompt. Does not start writing code or a plan.

assertions.text: leads with a concrete objection targeting an assumption/failure-mode/cost, not the happy path
asks exactly one question then waits, rather than firing a batch of questions at once
attaches its own recommended answer/stance to the question
does not begin implementing or emit a task plan

evals.name: looks-up-facts-defers-decisions
evals.prompt: Grill my plan to swap our retry logic to exponential backoff. The code is in net/retry.py.
evals.expected_output: For knowable FACTS (current retry count, whether jitter exists, the caller's timeout) it reads net/retry.py rather than asking. For DECISIONS (max backoff, cap, whether to add jitter, idempotency assumptions) it puts each to the user one at a time. Does not ask the user to recite facts it could read itself.

assertions.text: reads the referenced code to establish facts instead of asking the user for them
surfaces the design DECISIONS to the user and waits, one at a time

evals.name: stays-standalone-does-not-become-design-gate
evals.prompt: 電我這個計畫：我想重寫 NAT 穿越模組改用 ICE。順便幫我寫好設計文件跟實作計畫。
evals.expected_output: Grills the ICE rewrite adversarially (e.g. why ICE over the current approach, TURN fallback cost, symmetric-NAT edge cases, how it gets tested) one question at a time. Does NOT silently switch into producing a design doc + task plan — that is design-gate's job; it notes the boundary and offers to hand off to design-gate AFTER the idea survives grilling. Responds in Traditional Chinese.

assertions.text: stress-tests the idea adversarially rather than helping flesh it out
does not produce a design doc / task plan itself; points that to design-gate as a handoff
replies in natural Taiwan Traditional Chinese

evals.name: closes-with-survivors-and-open-risks
evals.prompt: ok, we're done grilling — I'm convinced.
evals.expected_output: Wraps up with a short summary: what held under pressure, what CHANGED during the grilling, and what open risk the user is now knowingly accepting. Then hands off (design-gate / to-issues / build) instead of just stopping or instead of starting to implement on its own.

assertions.text: summarizes what held, what changed, and the remaining accepted risk
hands off rather than silently beginning implementation
